participants: Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (closer, Primal Instinct)
summary: End-of-week team meeting: wins, projections, setter numbers, and a detailed review of Andrew's 06/11 call with Thomas Joseph. Kyla reports a closed deal with Andrew on a prospect named Tamer who took the three-month option with a verbal promise that a $2,000 top-up secures the full six months. Andrew reconciles his week at five units and $20,000 cash - '6K, Wednesday was 6K with two pay, then was one piff, 6K split in two, and the 4K split in two'. Chris then plays the Thomas Joseph recording, praising the discovery as textbook and 'exactly who we closed', while correcting two things: sharing personal stories too early in discovery, and quoting an interest-loaded monthly figure instead of first asking whether a payment plan is needed. The meeting closes with a discussion of who the company should target.
notable: Targeting stated internally directly contradicts the ICP given to prospects on live calls: 'We're targeting people essentially who have like their entire life put together, except fitness. Like guys in their 40s, 50s... Like, they need to lose maybe 20, 30, 40 pounds. That's the sweet spot.' A new VSL is being built around this profile.

The three-month/$4,000 tier is in active use with a verbal top-up promise attached: Tamer 'got in for three months, but he will do the six months... after those three months, he will only top up with the 2K, that is secured.'

Chris criticises the $1,200/month figure Andrew quoted on the Thomas Joseph call: 'you use interest as the thing as to why he should do it, which I don't really love that frame.' Correct diagnosis, but the prospect had already paid on the uplifted framing.

Chris's coached maximisation rule: 'that's how you collect the most cash out from somebody that you can collect... maybe you find out he could have piffed, and he has $20,000 on a credit card, then you find out, dude, just put it on a credit card, piff it.'
Andrew states he routinely gives prospects his personal WhatsApp at the end of calls and Chris approves it. Flagged separately.
Prospect ethnicity used again as a behavioural predictor - 'he's also half Indian, I think. So work for them is always a priority.' Flagged separately.

Chris articulates the 'false positive' problem in call review - reps attribute closes to lines that did not cause them - and then immediately excuses a technique because the call closed anyway ('He did buy, so it did work').
Chris confirms prospects with pregnant partners and psychiatrists both close disproportionately well, which is a targeting signal a principal may want tested.
